title: Listening & Reading
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah mempelajari kosakata dan struktur untuk mendeskripsikan benda-benda yang ditemukan di rumah.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 43-45
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will be able to understand and identify additional key vocabulary about bathrooms and the objects in them.
Learners will listen and understand people talking about bathrooms and the objects in them.
Learners will read and understand stories about homes.

details: Greet the students and ask about their feelings. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”
The teacher introduces himself/herself in front of the class.
Get to know the students by using the letter game.
The teacher writes down his/her name on the board (e.g. Susan)
Ask the student if their name starts with the shown letter (e.g. starts with S) and then they must stand up and introduce themselves. Continue with other letters.
Other alternatives to get to know the students: hot potato and throw the ball.
Ask students to look at the pictures and questions on page 43.
Tell them that they need to listen and circle the word that they hear in the audio.
Before listening, practice pronunciation of the words in task A. The teacher says the two vocabulary choices given for each number.
Play audio 5.3. If needed, the teacher can pause the audio after track 1 to check students’ understanding.
Ask students to check their answers with a partner and then check the answers together.

Play audio again and ask students to write down the sentences they hear in their notebooks (this is a simple dictation activity). Then show the audio script and ask students to correct their sentences.
This activity is for pronunciation practice.
Play audio 5.4 and encourage students to repeat the words loudly, and encourage them to try to copy the intonation they hear in the audio.
For variation, vocabulary drilling can be done in groups, pairs, loudly, quietly, etc.
In order to make vocabulary drilling more interesting, students could be guided to drill using different emotions (e.g. excited or surprised) or voices.

Students are going to complete task C, in which they need to describe to each other what they can see in the pictures of bathrooms (a-f), paying attention to the furniture and objects, and the color of those items.
Elicit responses from students, focusing on which objects they can see, and what color they are.
Tell students that they need to listen and draw a line from each person to their bathroom.
Play audio 5.5. If needed, the teacher can pause the audio after track 1 to check that the students understand how to
Ask students to look at the pictures on Student Book page 44-45.
Ask some specific questions about the pictures, for example, ‘How many people can you see?’, ‘Where are they?’
Giving some personal questions is also suggested to make it more relatable to students, for example, “Have you ever bought a gift for your mother?”
Ask students to look at task A on Student Book page 44.
Read the vocabulary choices from the boxes below, and ask students to repeat them.
Ask students to match the words to the correct pictures.
Before that, read the meanings in the white boxes aloud, and ask students to repeat them after you.
They need to draw lines to match the words to the pictures, and also lines to match the words to the definitions.
Do the first activity together as a class to make sure students understand what to do. Check the answers as a class.
Next, put students in pairs and ask them to answer the questions together.
Give students 3-4 minutes to complete the task.
Then ask some students to share their answers with the class. Answers will vary because these questions require students' own personal responses.
Tell students that they will listen and read the story. Play audio 5.6 and ask them to read the text silently.
Next, play the audio again and ask students to read the text aloud, following the audio. Ask if there are any questions about the language in the text.

As a way to make the reading session more engaging, teachers could divide the class into several groups and assign each group to read one paragraph alternately in different ways (e.g. loudly or quietly).
Now, students will write the numbers 1-6 in the boxes to put the story events in order from first to last.
The first question can be done together as a class to make sure students know what to do.
Then, they can complete the task in pairs or by themselves.
Ask students to check their answers with a friend.
Check the answers as a class. Write the answers on the board.
Tell students to practice asking and answering the completed questions in Reading D together. First, Student A asks the questions and Student B answers them. Then switch the role.
Now ask students to look at task E.
Instruct them to discuss the questions in groups of three or four students.
After about 6-8 minutes, elicit some answers for each question from each group.
This activity could be done if there is more time.
Ask students to write two of their own True/ False statements about the reading text in their notebooks.

Put students in pairs and ask them to show each other their True/ False statements. Students must say either True or False about their partner’s statements. Then, each student should say whether the answer is correct or incorrect.
Ask around five individual students to write one of their T/F statements on the whiteboard.
Then ask the whole class to give their answers to each statement by putting their thumbs up if the statement is True, or thumbs down if the statement is False.
The students who wrote their statements on the board should tell the class the correct answers and explain why.
Wrap up the class by asking the students something  that they want to try to show care and love to their beloved ones.
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: ketepatan jawaban tugas listening (menomori/menjodohkan/melengkapi).
Pertanyaan pemahaman bacaan (literal & inferensial) dan pembahasan bersama.
reflectionStudent: Apa hal baru yang kamu pelajari hari ini?
Bagian mana yang paling mudah dan paling sulit bagimu? Mengapa?
Kalimat bahasa Inggris apa yang sudah bisa kamu ucapkan dengan percaya diri?
Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
Berapa persen instruksi kelas yang disampaikan dalam bahasa Inggris?
Peserta didik mana yang memerlukan pendampingan atau pengayaan?
